item.title: Trump's immigration crackdown hits US military families; over 50 spouses detained
item.description: Dozens of parents and spouses of US service members face detention and deportation. This marks a significant shift from prior bipartisan immigration policies for military families. Many are detained during routine immigration status adjustment appointments. The Department of Homeland Security states military service does not exempt violations of immigration laws. These detentions negatively impact military readiness and family stability.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: World C'ships: Shetty to face top-ranked Shi Yuqi in opener - full draw
item.description: Ayush Shetty will get the chance to improve his win-loss record against top-ranked Chinese shuttler Shi Yuqi in the first round of the 2026 BWF World Championships in New Delhi that begin on August 17. PV Sindhu, chasing her sixth medal, could face top seed and nemesis An Se Young only in the semi-final.
item.dc:creator: TANUJ LAKHINA

item.title: 'May be jailed, but I’ll return to Bangladesh this December,' says Sheikh Hasina
item.description: Sheikh Hasina declared she is not afraid of arrest upon her return to Bangladesh in December. She stated her return is for the nation's future and to set it on the right track. Dhaka reacted sharply, calling her an absconding convicted genocider and expressing regret over the event. Hasina described the July Uprising as a regime change operation orchestrated by a mastermind.
item.dc:creator: AHSAN TASNIM

item.title: OpenAI's Greg Brockman gives millions to save eagles Jackie and Shadow's home
item.description: Greg Brockman and his wife Anna donated five point five million dollars to save shoreline forest. This significant contribution helped secure ten million dollars for land conservation efforts. The land, which is home to rare species, will now be protected from development. Over twenty-five thousand small donors also contributed to the successful fundraising campaign. Meanwhile, the eagle matriarch Jackie faces an uncertain health prognosis.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Meta apologises for ‘error in restricting PM’s video’
item.description: Meta's CEO Mark Zuckerberg formally apologized to the Indian government over several operational missteps, including issues with paid content amplification. The acknowledgment of these errors comes as officials expressed concerns over the potential loss of safe harbor protection for the platform. As the government reassesses its child online safety regulations, Meta committed to implementing necessary corrective actions to address these concerns.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: With all eyes on delimitation & FCRA, monsoon session sinks deeper into deadlock
item.description: Parliament has hit yet another impasse as the opposition protests continue for the thirteenth day. Despite this, the government succeeded in passing important legislation, including the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill and a bill concerning Supreme Court judges. In an effort to resolve the deadlock, minister Kiren Rijiju met with opposition figures, while Prime Minister Modi focused on discussing strategies with BJP Members of Parliament.
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV SINGH

item.title: Centre renews bid for delimitation bill as Rijiju reaches out to Rahul Gandhi
item.description: The government is pushing its delimitation legislation to increase Lok Sabha seats. This bill also proposes one-third reservation for women starting in 2029. Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi rejected the government's outreach for support. The government may reintroduce the Constitution amendment bill soon. Discussions continue regarding the Foreign Contributions Regulation Amendment Bill.
item.dc:creator: KUMAR RAKESH

item.title: DHS plan hints at higher H1B, L1 visa fees for large companies
item.description: The US government plans to expand an additional fee for certain visa petitions. This fee currently applies to initial H-1B and L-1 visa grants. The proposed change will extend this charge to petitions for extensions of stay. Companies with over fifty employees and a majority on these visas will be affected. This expansion aims to fund biometric entry-exit systems and other government programs.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Rajya Sabha passes by voice vote bill to raise Supreme Court judge strength
item.description: The Rajya Sabha approved a bill to increase the Supreme Court's judge count. This legislation replaces an ordinance that raised the sanctioned strength to thirty-eight judges. The bill's passage aims to expedite case disposal and enhance judicial efficiency. It will also provide the Chief Justice greater flexibility in forming constitution benches. India anticipates its first woman Chief Justice in the near future.
item.dc:creator: ATUL MATHUR

item.title: Meet Seungah Chung, who used 200 ants to reveal how they navigate
item.description: A bright young student embarked on a fascinating ant navigation experiment fueled by her natural curiosity. Through her meticulous research, she uncovered that ants primarily depend on visual markers for navigation. This groundbreaking project garnered her acclaim at a well-regarded science competition, showcasing the potential of such findings to inspire the development of innovative robots and autonomous systems.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: Kazakhstan releases first wild tiger in 70 years after extinction
item.description: Kazakhstan has released adult Amur tigers into the wild after a 70-year absence. This reintroduction follows extensive habitat preparation and prey population restoration efforts. Scientists confirmed the genetic similarity between extinct Turanian and current Amur tiger populations. The country has implemented a comprehensive conflict-prevention system for human-tiger coexistence. This significant conservation initiative aims to re-establish tigers in their historic Central Asian range.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: Priscilla Chan founded a school in 2016; 10 yrs later, it closed after $125m funding
item.description: The Primary School, a tuition-free institution, will close in June after a decade of operation. This school provided education, healthcare, and family support to low-income children. The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative will not continue funding beyond the upcoming academic year. Academic results remained below state averages, prompting the board's decision. The initiative pledged fifty million dollars to aid the transition for affected students.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Pradeep Rawat's son Vikramaditya recalls actor's heartbreaking final moments
item.description: Veteran actor Pradeep Rawat's son, Vikramaditya, broke down as he recalled his father's final moments during the actor's last rites held at Oshiwara Crematorium in Mumbai on Wednesday. Speaking to the media after bidding an emotional farewell to his father, Vikramaditya shared how the family initially believed the actor was suffering from a minor stomach infection before doctors diagnosed him with an aggressive and rare form of blood cancer.

item.title: How Cristiano Ronaldo overcame poverty and loss to become a football legend
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo’s journey is about much more than football. From growing up in poverty and leaving home at 12 to losing his father before achieving global success, every challenge shaped the player he became. His story reminds people that discipline, sacrifice and love for family can help overcome even the hardest moments and turn dreams into reality.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: How Travis Kelce is transforming lives beyond football in Kansas City
item.description: Kansas City Chiefs star Travis Kelce supports local children and families. He partnered with Kodiak to provide twenty-five thousand hot meals. Kelce also invested in Operation Breakthrough, a Kansas City nonprofit. His Eighty-Seven & Running Foundation supports youth programs and career exploration. This initiative offers practical skills and a safe space for students.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Meet Brock Lesnar's family: Wife Sable, children, parents and siblings
item.description: Brock Lesnar, the WWE legend, leads a private family life with his wife Sable. They share two sons, Turk and Duke, who play competitive hockey. Lesnar also has twins, Mya and Luke, from a previous relationship. Mya excels in college shot put while Luke wrestles competitively. Raised on a South Dakota dairy farm, Lesnar credits his parents for his strong work ethic.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Black Sea attack: Merchant Navy officer's family refuses cremation, seeks martyr status
item.description: Following a brutal attack in the Black Sea, the remains of Merchant Navy chief officer Sagar Gupta were brought back to Kanpur. His family, deeply affected by the loss, has declared they will not conduct any last rites until specific demands are fulfilled, including martyr recognition, financial compensation, and employment for his widow.
item.dc:creator: PRACHI KUMAWAT

item.title: Jiya Shankar announces engagement to Kaaran Dhanak; shares dreamy proposal pics
item.description: Jiya Shankar from Bigg Boss OTT 2 has officially shared the joyous news of her engagement to Kaaran Dhanak. She celebrated this special milestone by posting their heartfelt proposal pictures on social media. The actress expressed her overwhelming love for her fiancé, a US-based entrepreneur, emphasizing their relationship as a captivating adventure akin to her favorite romantic comedy.

item.title: Hyderabad CA dies by suicide by inhaling helium over 'gaming losses'
item.description: In Siddipet, a chartered accountant tragically took his own life, burdened by heavy gambling losses. Employing helium gas, a method learned from online tutorials, he was discovered in a hotel room after the staff notified the authorities. His suicide note revealed the anguish linked to his financial plight, despite family support and efforts to sell his property.

item.title: Commercial plane takes off as Trump’s helicopter nears airport; FAA investigates
item.description: An investigation by the Federal Aviation Administration has been initiated concerning a potential safety breach. A commercial aircraft took off just as President Trump’s helicopter was nearing Reagan National Airport, leading to a brief loss of separation. Following a tragic midair collision in 2025, stricter regulations have been enforced. The White House assured that the President’s safety was never compromised.
item.dc:creator: TRISHA MAHAJAN

item.title: Inside Marilyn Monroe's California home where the Hollywood icon spent her final days
item.description: Marilyn Monroe's former Los Angeles home, a Spanish-style residence, remains a significant cultural landmark today. The property was acquired by new owners with plans for demolition in 2023. However, the L.A. City Council designated the house a Historic Cultural Monument, halting demolition. The owners then sued the city, claiming an unconstitutional taking of their private property. A court dismissed the case, but the owners reportedly amended their complaint.
item.dc:creator: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK

item.title: 'I worked tirelessly while staying in Pakistan': Nadeem blames cold for CWG poor show
item.description: Pakistan’s Olympic javelin champion Arshad Nadeem blamed Glasgow’s cold weather for his ninth-place Commonwealth Games finish, saying it stiffened his body and affected his run-up. Despite the setback, he urged fans not to lose faith and promised a strong comeback. Nadeem’s next challenge is the Lausanne Diamond League on August 21, where he will face Neeraj Chopra.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: Cong vs Cong in Punjab: With 'sleeper cell' warning, party puts Channi camp on notice
item.description: Amid rising infighting, the Congress party has issued a stern warning to Punjab's dissenters regarding their involvement with internal 'sleeper cells.' Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, the state president, has promised that party members acting against Congress will face consequences, with no tickets granted to them. The situation intensifies as Charanjit Singh Channi's supporters openly question the leadership, complicating the party's position in the face of a multi-dimensional electoral challenge in assembly elections early next year.
item.dc:creator: KUNAL VARMA

item.title: Indian-American Congressman Shri Thanedar loses Democratic primary in Michigan
item.description: Shri Thanedar lost the Michigan Democratic primary to Donavan McKinney. McKinney secured victory with support from the party's progressive wing. Thanedar acknowledged the socialist movement's influence on the election outcome. His defeat may reduce Indian-American representation in the House. Thanedar expressed gratitude for his service and plans to remain active.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: Suspected sulphur dioxide leak kills 3 factory workers in Karnataka's Yadgir
item.description: A catastrophic event unfolded in Yadgir district early Wednesday as a suspected sulphur dioxide leak claimed the lives of three workers and left two others injured. Reports suggest that the chemical leak caused suffocation among the employees present. The victims were migrant laborers hailing from Telangana and Madhya Pradesh, and the survivors are now under medical care at a nearby hospital.

item.description: Actor R Madhavan shared his joy for his friend Vijay, now in the Chief Minister's role, while firmly stating that he has no ambitions in politics. He described politics as a complicated affair and expressed no desire to take on such responsibilities. Additionally, Madhavan talked about his role in 'GDN,' where he will portray inventor G. D.

item.title: Rupee hits 1-month closing high despite RBI pause; sliding oil prices help
item.description: The currency opened 0.5% stronger at 94.92 against the US dollar, its highest level since July 1. It later gave up nearly half of its early advance to settle at 95.1175 per dollar, its strongest closing level since July 7.
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: Lock Upp 2 Grand Finale: Shreya Kalra wins by 7 votes, bags Rs 1 crore
item.description: Shreya Kalra has triumphed in the electrifying finale of Lock Upp 2, being crowned the champion along with a lucrative cash prize of one crore rupees. Shivangi Joshi finished as the first runner-up in a nail-biting race where only seven votes distinguished the two finalists. As the news broke, fans expressed a spectrum of emotions, praising Kalra's accomplishment while showing admiration for Joshi's remarkable journey in the competition.
